checked_sources: Independent derivation by cap minimization and differentiation of the implicit optimality equation
correctness.rationale: The strictly convex coercive objective has a unique minimizer. Soft thresholding at p=1 and radial shrinkage at p=2 compose by threshold addition, including extinction. At p=∞ one can directly constrain the output to a cap λ: within [−λ,λ]^n the least-squares optimizer clips coordinates, and minimizing over λ≥0 gives sum_i(|x_i|−λ)_+=t until extinction at t=||x||_1. A second clipping removes the additional mass s, so its final cap solves the single clipping equation at s+t (or the output is zero). For finite p>1, the implicit equation z+h∇f(z)=x has a jointly smooth local solution around (0,u), with first two h-derivatives at zero −g and 2Hg. The expansion is valid also at the nearby first-step point. Composition contributes 3Hg in order h² compared with 4Hg for the step 2h. Direct differentiation at u gives (Hg)_1=(p−1)(n−1+2^p)^(2/p−3)(2^p−2^(2p−2)). The difference is the negative of this coefficient; it is nonzero except at p=2 and has the stated signs. The n=1 case correctly reduces to the absolute-value map for all p.
residual_risks: The Taylor estimate is local near the positive witness and fixed in n and p; no uniform constant or finite-h sign globally in x is proved.

evidence: BBCN Theorem 4.5 assumes p(t)∈∂J(p(t)) along the flow, then yields flow/variational equivalence; its L¹ and L∞ examples cover the endpoint method. Theorem 4.4 is an iff for the eigenvector property, not a converse characterization of resolvent time-additivity.

Bërdëllima–Steidl obtain a flow semigroup by limits of repeated short resolvent steps. The distinct group-penalty record calculates the identical −H∇F second-order obstruction, but its classification selects disjoint coordinate groups from finite positive sums of Euclidean block norms.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The availability of an abstract flow semigroup, or sufficiency of a flow eigenvector condition, cannot by itself imply failure of finite-step composition at an excluded exponent. On any coordinate two-plane a positive sum of coordinate Euclidean block norms restricts to a|x|+b|y|+c√(x²+y²). A finite ℓ_p norm with p>1 is differentiable at the nonzero axes, forcing a=b=0; normalization then requires c=1, and evaluation at (1,1) forces p=2. The nonendpoint classification is therefore not a special case of the published group theorem.

value.rationale: A complete answer for the basic ℓ_p scale distinguishes when one Euclidean proximal step really is a time semigroup step, a stronger condition than existence of the associated flow. One witness covers every excluded exponent, and the signed leading defect distinguishes the two sides of p=2. This is useful as a worked exact norm-family classification and diagnostic; the standalone Taylor formula and the positive endpoint shrinkages are not the value claim.
residual_risks: Does not classify arbitrary norms or quantify a global splitting error for practical finite step sizes.
